title: Prompt-Payment Interest Owed on Late-Paid GAP Claims
content:
# Prompt-payment interest owed on a late-paid GAP balance line

**Schedule.** Under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda, a paid GAP balance line that was paid late after the insurer's settlement carries late-payment interest owed on it. In an overpayment recovery, that interest is set against the overpayment. The test reads the waiver's most recent paid GAP balance line: the insurer's settlement date recorded on it, the date it was paid, and the amount paid. Days are counted in calendar days from the settlement date (day 0). The claim payment period is 30 calendar days for every tier, so twice that period is 60 days.

| The line was paid | Yearly late-payment rate |
|---|---|
| more than 60 calendar days after the settlement date | 0.12 (12 percent) |
| more than 30 but no more than 60 calendar days after the settlement date | 0.08 (8 percent) |
| within 30 calendar days of the settlement date | none owed |

**Interest owed.** The late-payment interest owed is the amount paid on the line times the yearly rate times the calendar days past the 30-day claim payment period after the settlement date, divided by 365, rounded half up to the cent. It is set against the overpayment, but it never takes the reversal below one half of the overpayment.

### Worked example (hypothetical figures)

The paid line paid 2,210.00.

| Paid on | Days past 30 | Rate | Interest owed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 30 | 0 | none | 0.00 |
| Day 48 | 18 | 0.08 | 2,210.00 times 0.08 times 18 divided by 365, which is 8.72 |
| Day 60 | 30 | 0.08 | 14.53 |
| Day 61 | 31 | 0.12 | 22.52 |
| Day 71 | 41 | 0.12 | 29.79 |

With an overpayment of 40.00 and interest owed of 29.79, the reversal is 20.00, half of the overpayment.
